summary: Refreshed after merging main at eb48c12 (no change to this PR's own code; conflicts only in CHANGELOG, VERSION, ci.yml, operations/reference docs and the ADR index). Router 0.41.0 implements ADR-0117 (waker and release-source interfaces) with ADR-0124 (transport rules). Two new outbound destinations: (1) the http_webhook waker POSTs a fixed body {event, node, mac} to a URL from config.yaml; (2) release_source: document GETs a neutral release document. Both go through values.egress_url (ADR-0048 rules: final URL, HTTPS or HTTP to literal 127.0.0.1/::1 only, no userinfo/query/fragment) and refuse 3xx without following (allow_redirects=False), with total timeouts (webhook 1-60 s, document 20 s), trust_env off. Traced callers: proxy._wake_or_refuse -> wakers.wake (shared wait/poll loop, unchanged cadence and cooldown for wol), scheduler.wakeable_for -> wakers.can_wake (wol eligibility identical to `n.wol and n.mac`), registry.node_policy and node_spec_from_entry (B2: the admin policy may only name 'wol' or a configured waker; URL and token_env are config-file only, consistent with ADR-0016), settings.EDITABLE (release_source added as a choice beside the already UI-editable release_url; UI writes are validated by the probe parse in write_overrides, so a document URL must pass egress_url there too), ollamaupdate.check_latest -> _fetch_document/parse_document -> LATEST -> order_update (B8: the order still carries only version, canonical archive name, sha256 and size; the agent downloads from its own ollama_update.source and refuses a hash that differs from that source's sha256sum.txt, agent TestOllamaUpdateRun; downgrade refusals of ADR-0073 unchanged). Secrets/logs (B9): the bearer token is read from the environment at call time and never logged; a configured but empty token fails closed without a request; log lines carry only the receiver host and exception class, never the URL path (a webhook ID can be a secret). No command execution was added; command/ipmi kinds are refused at load. Found and fixed during review: a deeply nested release document under the size cap raised RecursionError past the JSON boundary (now caught, test added); an OS error from the magic-packet socket used to escape as an exception (now a wake_send_failed fact, socket closed).

tests.evidence: 18 tests: magic packet bytes/addresses/port 9 and SO_BROADCAST pinned, WOL cadence every retry_interval_s, cooldown, eligibility as before; webhook fixed body + bearer token, missing token sends nothing, 301/302/303/307/308 refused and target never contacted, HTTP 500 refused, 0.5 s timeout while another coroutine keeps running, unreachable port; config refusals (plain HTTP non-loopback, localhost, query, fragment, userinfo, ftp, bad port, command/ipmi kinds, name wol, unknown key, token value instead of env name, timeout range/type, repeat type) and policy refusal of a URL as waker.

10 tests: document equals GitHub source output for the same release; redirect refused (target not fetched), oversized with and without Content-Length, timeout, HTTP 404, invalid JSON, invalid UTF-8, 30000-deep nesting (fails without the RecursionError catch, checked), every malformed field; release_source/release_url refused at config load for http non-loopback, query, empty URL, unknown kind.

limitations: The configured destinations are trusted operator input: DNS of the configured host is not pinned, so a host whose name resolves into the LAN is reachable by design (no redirect can add a second destination).
The pre-existing github release source still follows redirects and has no size cap (unchanged; GitHub serves sha256sum.txt through a redirect). Its JSON comes from api.github.com by default.

release_url stays editable from the web UI as before; with release_source document an admin session can point the router at another document, which can only select a version/hash that the agent then verifies against its own source (B2 admin trust, TM-03).
/admin/config shows the configured webhook URL to admins like other configuration values; a webhook ID embedded in the path is visible there (not in logs).
No native ipmi waker (deferred); no UI control for the waker choice yet (config file and policy API only).
Webhook and document were exercised against loopback test servers only; no real Home Assistant/ioBroker/openHAB receiver or mirror was contacted.
PostgreSQL integrations were not run; no session/memory/storage code changed.
